title: Contained AppContainer child launch qualification
objective: Prove on native Windows CI that Cotra can create a zero-capability AppContainer child suspended, assign it to a kill-on-close Job Object before resume, verify its AppContainer token and Job membership, resume it, observe bounded completion, and clean up without exposing external EXECUTE authority.

include: fixed system executable resolved from the Windows system directory without caller-controlled path variables
fixed-name scrubbed Unicode child environment including AppContainer profile roots
bounded child wait and exit-code evidence

authority_delta.filesystem: No workspace grant; the Windows CI probe launches only the fixed system cmd.exe child and creates/deletes a temporary AppContainer profile
authority_delta.process: Internal Windows qualification child only; no remote or MCP process authority
authority_delta.secrets: Child receives only a fixed allowlist of non-secret Windows path/platform variables required for AppContainer launch; arbitrary caller environment variables and Cotra/tunnel secrets are not inherited

invariants: The child executable is the fixed cmd.exe name under the operating system directory returned by GetSystemDirectoryW, not a path derived from caller environment
The child token is verified as AppContainer before resume
The child is assigned to the Cotra Job Object and IsProcessInJob is true before resume
The AppContainer is created with zero capabilities
The child receives no inherited handles and only the fixed safe-name environment allowlist; arbitrary caller variables and secrets are excluded
Failure after child creation performs best-effort termination
Temporary AppContainer profile and Win32 handles are cleaned up
process.spawn and PowerShell remain absent from policy and MCP

acceptance.claim: Native Windows test creates a zero-capability AppContainer process suspended.
TokenIsAppContainer is nonzero for the suspended child.
AssignProcessToJobObject succeeds and IsProcessInJob confirms membership before ResumeThread.
The child resumes, exits within the bounded timeout, and exit code is recorded.
Temporary profile and process/thread/job/attribute-list resources are cleaned up.
Non-Windows builds remain cfg-isolated from Win32 linkage.
Exact-head Windows/Ubuntu Rust, Node, and Governance CI pass.

done_when: The suspended-create -> AppContainer verification -> Job assignment -> resume -> bounded completion sequence is proven on Windows CI and merged with post-merge verification. External EXECUTE authority remains a successor grain.
